title: Cure Compiler
one_liner: See how 'approve the process, not the drug' shrinks the bill for curing 5,000 diseases from trillions to billions.
speaker: Dave Blundin (via an agent's thought experiment)
context: Dave's agent argued that 5,000 drugs at about $2B each is unaffordable. Approve a gene-editing platform once and each new disease becomes a sequence change costing about $2M. The bottlenecks are delivery to tissues, late diagnosis, and too few geneticists.
demo: A big counter shows the total cost of curing 5,000 diseases. A slider sets the cost per added disease, from $2B down to $2M, and the counter drops from $10 trillion toward $10 billion. A body map lights up the tissues where delivery works per the note (liver, blood, eye) and greys out kidney and most of the brain. Visitors can mark a tissue as 'unlocked' to see how many simulated diseases become reachable. A side gauge compares the number of geneticists to the number of patients.
data_plan: A bundled dataset of the episode's stated figures. Disease counts per tissue are clearly labelled simulated illustrative data.
risks: This was a thought experiment voiced by an AI avatar, not established fact, and the page must say so. It is not medical information about any disease. Per-tissue disease counts are invented for illustration and must be labelled.
